explain.say: Mrs Dalloway said she would buy the flowers herself. With that line Virginia Woolf opens her 1925 novel, set on one day in June 1923 in London. A gentle note: the book deals with war trauma and suicide. The web shows Clarissa Dalloway, who gives a party tonight, and a stranger whose life runs alongside hers.

explain.say: Follow the day. Clarissa walks through Westminster buying flowers; her old love Peter Walsh drops by. Every hour Big Ben strikes, and Woolf uses the sound to jump from one mind to another across the city. That is how she links people who never meet. What is the clock doing to time in this book?

explain.say: Now look at Septimus Warren Smith, a young veteran of the First World War with shell shock, what we would now call post-traumatic stress. He sees his dead friend Evans and hears birds sing in Greek. His wife Rezia is desperate, and the doctors tell him to rest and stop thinking about himself. How might he feel, hearing that?

explain.say: Woolf said Septimus was meant to be Clarissa's double. On the left, a wealthy hostess who chose a safe marriage; on the right, a clerk broken by war. When a doctor arrives to take him away, Septimus ends his life. Woolf herself had suffered breakdowns and harsh treatments. What do these two share?

At the party, Dr Bradshaw's wife mentions the young man's death. Clarissa slips away, thinks about him, feels she understands, and then returns to her guests. Woolf called her method tunnelling: digging caves behind each character that connect. Wonderful work. Challenge: what does Clarissa's return to the party say about choosing life?

faq.q: Why is Septimus in Mrs Dalloway?
faq.a: He brings the war into a society novel. His trauma shadows Clarissa's day, and Woolf said she intended him as Clarissa's double, showing the despair her party hides.

faq.q: What is the role of Big Ben in Mrs Dalloway?
faq.a: Its striking marks the hours and lets Woolf move between characters who hear it at the same moment. It stands for public clock time against the private time of memory.

faq.q: Do Clarissa and Septimus ever meet?
faq.a: Never. They are linked by shared sights and sounds, such as Big Ben, a car and an aeroplane, and Clarissa hears of his death at her party and feels a strange kinship.

faq.q: How does Woolf criticise doctors in Mrs Dalloway?
faq.a: Dr Holmes dismisses Septimus's illness and Sir William Bradshaw prescribes isolation and a sense of proportion, crushing him. Woolf drew on her own experience of treatment for mental illness.
Her diary phrase for digging out caves of memory behind her characters, so that the past opens up inside the present day and the caves connect between people.

facts: Mrs Dalloway was published in May 1925.
Woolf's working title was The Hours, later used by Michael Cunningham for his 1998 novel.
The novel takes place on a single day in June 1923.
